status: DERIVED AND CONFIRMED — the singularity is a gauge, and the quotient makes the closed form a one-line normalisation
claim: M_l = Wn'Wn is singular (rank 2560 < 9216) because ker(M) = ker(Wn) are dose combinations with zero residual effect. d* = p50 Wn' gradPhi lies in range(Wn'), so d*'u = 0 on the kernel: the kernel directions cost nothing AND gain nothing, so the constrained linear problem is bounded and nothing is lost. Quotient by the kernel (parameterise v = Wn u in R^2560, where the budget is the plain Euclidean norm) and the closed form collapses to v* = b * gradPhi/||gradPhi||.

confirmation.reading: the M^-1 lift reproduces the residual-space gradient EXACTLY (1.0000), while the naive dose-space gradient is 12-24 degrees off. So the committed 36-43% gain of u_M over u_g is not a mystery: it is 1/cos, and 1/0.76 = 1.32 at layer 13 against a measured 1.36-1.43.

why_not_ridge: A ridge lambda prices the gauge (it charges lambda*||u||^2 for directions whose residual effect is zero), so it changes the optimum. The pinv/min-norm lift does not: the optimum in the quotient space is unchanged, and the min-norm rule only fixes which representative is reported. Ridge is a distortion here, not a cure.
what_it_does_not_fix: Positions. u = Wn^+ v* is ONE representative; the admissible family is u + ker(Wn), 6656-dimensional per layer. So 'position' is a representative, not an object, and any position claim must be made in the quotient or with a stated rule. The min-norm rule (L2 in dose space) picks the LEAST sparse representative, while community selectors pick sparse ones - so part of the 1.7% position overlap is an artifact of representative choice.
consequences: the deliverable can be restated with no 9216^2 object at all: v* is 2560 numbers per layer from one backward; the 10.9 GB Gram and the 6-minute solve are unnecessary

sparsity (K positions) is a resource ORTHOGONAL to the residual-norm budget; in the quotient space the well-posed question is 'the sparsest representative of v*', which is a linear-algebra problem, not a tuning problem
'directions reproducible, positions not' (93.4% sign agreement, 1.7% exact overlap) is exactly what non-uniqueness predicts, and the fair comparison is in the quotient space, not on position lists
